patch_description: Instead of rewarding several two-hop paths independently, this design treats them as competing routing options for each origin-destination pair. It repeatedly estimates a soft traffic split and raises prices on links and transit nodes with higher estimated load. The final sparse QUBO keeps the direct option and the two best-priced two-hop alternatives; their rewards share a per-demand budget, limiting the double-counting that can make broad path rewards misleading. A modest reciprocal-link cost is retained as a structural tie-breaker.
